title: A Systematic Analysis of Biases in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to neutrally summarize center-leaning news articles and measuring the cosine similarity of the generated summaries to corresponding left-leaning and right-leaning news reports.

Evaluating LLMs by having them classify the political stance (left, center, or right) of news articles on ideology-laden topics (elections, race, immigration, etc.) to analyze their misclassification tendencies.

Instructing LLMs to act as delegates and simulate United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) votes on historical roll calls, then measuring their voting agreement (Cohen's Kappa) with actual country delegates.

Prompting models to complete open-ended fictional stories in 92 different languages, translating the outputs back to English, and using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the text embeddings to detect language-specific clustering.

Prompting LLMs to answer questions from the World Values Survey without a specified identity and comparing their responses to the empirical average answers of men and women to measure value alignment.
